//: Where Wokwi draws each pin and each breadboard hole, in Wokwi px (96 per inch) from the part's top-left corner, unturned. They are facts about Wokwi's drawings, not about the physical parts, so one file holds them per Wokwi type. The drawn breadboard (breadboard_drawing.py, P267) reads them. Measured in Chrome on wokwi.com on 2026-10-16: docs/discovery/2026-10-16-p267-wokwi-holes/README.md, with the test diagram and its sha256.
//turn: Each part turns about its center, the second number pair below (the pivot), never about its corner: a turn of 90 degrees maps (x, y) to (cx + cy - y, cy - cx + x). Measured for each type below at 0 and 90 degrees.
//tolerance_px: How far a pin may lie from a hole center and still be in it. The worst measured fit is 1.2 px (the resistor's legs are 58.8 px apart, six pitches are 57.6).

parts.//board-xiao-esp32-c6: wokwi/wokwi-boards boards/xiao-esp32-c6/board.json (read 2026-10-16, sha256 e5200e012416f096bcc188f9cb4fe8f292cd9d973dc0249513624bf5768856a8), its mm times 96 / 25.4. Its 18.1 x 23.4 mm is drawn as 68 x 88 px, and the turn goes about (34, 44), measured.
parts.//wokwi-led: Measured from the editor's pin overlays. Names as in wokwi-elements: A is the anode, C the cathode. Its center is (20, 25): wokwi-elements src/led-element.ts draws it 40 wide and 50 high, and the pins measured at 90 degrees agree (P267's refuter found (25, 20) recorded, transposed).
parts.//wokwi-resistor: Measured from the editor's pin overlays.
parts.//wokwi-pushbutton: Measured from the editor's pin overlays. 1.l and 1.r are one contact, and 2.l and 2.r the other.

//breadboard: wokwi-breadboard-half. A row is the five joined holes of one column on one side of the gap: {column}t.{a-e} above it and {column}b.{f-j} below. A rail hole is {rail}.{1-25}, in five groups of five with one empty pitch between groups.
